newsitem.title: FRANCE: Lafarge 1996 profits slide, sees strong 97.
newsitem.headline: Lafarge 1996 profits slide, sees strong 97.

text.p: French building materials group Lafarge said on Wednesday net profits fell more than 21 percent in 1996 but there would be a big profit improvement this year, based on an expected rise in sales of more than 10 percent.
Lafarge said net attributable profit was 1.85 billion francs in 1996, down from 2.35 billion in 1995, while its operating profit rose 3.2 percent and sales climbed 6.2 percent.

Lafarge chairman Bertrand Collomb said its growth strategy had raised both sales and operating profit in 1996 and its ongoing policy of expanding and strengthening its presence in international markets boded well for the future.
"And from 1997, I expect a strong increase in our profits," Collomb said in a results statement.
Lafarge said it expected 1997 turnover to be about 39 billion francs, up more than 10 percent from 35.2 billion.
Collomb told a news conference although the proportion of the group's sales in France had fallen from nearly 50 percent in 1988 to 32 percent now, the proportion of French sales was still too high.

Shares in Lafarge climbed more than two percent in a falling stockmarket on Wednesday as analysts focused on the better than expected operating results and the forecast for higher profits in 1997, rather than the drop in profits.
Fears of a drop in profit had sent Lafarge shares tumbling more than three percent on Tuesday.
Given the share's weak performance recently, "it's a good share to play on the economic recovery in Europe," a portfolio manager said.
Lafarge said the 18 percent rise in investment to seven billion francs had been driven mainly by spending in Europe and that it planned to invest a further six to eight billion francs in 1997.
